display.purpose: Wordmark, panel titles, and every numeral in the app via .font-numeral (tabular figures) — counters must not reflow their own width as they tick.

body.purpose: Prose, rule explanations, captions. Deliberately unremarkable so it never competes with adjacent numerals.

label.purpose: .label-micro — field labels and micro-headers inside a panel. Rationed to one per logical group.

mono.purpose: Connection codes, state hashes, cell notation — read character-by-character and pasted accurately. Not preloaded; never appears in a first paint.

shadows.name: rule-edge
shadows.purpose: Marks the active player's card. A line, not a lift — never combined with a blurred shadow.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: The one floating surface in the whole system: the native <dialog> (How to Play). Nothing else gets this.

motion.name: tremble
motion.purpose: The only ambient/looping motion in the app. A cell one orb from firing shakes because it genuinely is about to — never decorative.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The win moment. The one place the app is allowed to be pleased with itself; never a loop.

motion.name: burst
motion.purpose: A cell releasing its orbs; scales past the cell edge so overlapping generations read as one wave.

motion.name: claim
motion.purpose: A cell changing hands, washed in the capturing player's color.

motion.name: arrive
motion.purpose: Orbs entering a cell — small enough to register as weight, not bounce.

motion.name: ripple-step
motion.value: 22ms per Manhattan-distance step, capped at 6 steps
motion.purpose: Per-cell delay (not duration) that makes a cascade generation propagate outward from the triggering move rather than flashing simultaneously.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled, solid action on a page of hairlines — never more than one visible at a time.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--color-trace, #1F2421); color: var(--color-chart, #EDEAE3); border: 1px solid var(--color-trace, #1F2421); border-radius: 0; padding: 8px 24px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-trace, #1F2421); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Outlined action — the default for anything that isn't the single primary CTA.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: transparent; color: var(--color-trace, #1F2421); border: 1px solid rgb(31 36 33 / 0.32); border-radius: 0; padding: 6px 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.2s, border-color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #E3DFD5; border-color: var(--color-trace, #1F2421); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-trace, #1F2421); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: The system's one-of-N choice pattern (speed, difficulty, on/off) — equal-width buttons sharing one border, active option filled.
components.css: .ds-segmented { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); border: 1px solid rgb(31 36 33 / 0.32); } .ds-segmented-item { background: transparent; color: var(--color-trace, #1F2421); border: none; border-radius: 0; padding: 6px 4px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; min-height: 2.25rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-segmented-item:hover { background: #E3DFD5; } .ds-segmented-item.is-active { background: var(--color-trace, #1F2421); color: var(--color-chart, #EDEAE3); }

components.name: Panel Cluster
components.description: Groups related instrument readouts under one titled unit so a long HUD rail reads as sections, not a flat list.
components.css: .ds-cluster { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; border: 1px solid rgb(31 36 33 / 0.2); background: rgb(227 223 213 / 0.3); border-radius: 0; padding: 12px; } .ds-cluster-title { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--color-trace, #1F2421); margin: 0; } .ds-cluster-row { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; margin: 0; } .ds-label { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; color: #5E635E; } .ds-numeral { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Player Card
components.description: Whose turn it is, with shape and color both carrying identity. Active state is an ink-weight border and an inset rule-edge, never hue alone.
components.html: Jingga2
components.css: .ds-player-card { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; border: 1px solid rgb(31 36 33 / 0.2); border-radius: 0; padding: 8px 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; transition: background-color 0.2s, border-color 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s; } .ds-player-card.is-active { border-color: var(--color-trace, #1F2421); background: #E3DFD5; box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 0 currentColor; } .ds-player-name { font-weight: 500; } .ds-player-count { margin-left: auto; font-size: 18px; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Labeled-above field, numeral font for numeric values, no radius.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; } .ds-input { background: var(--color-chart, #EDEAE3); color: var(--color-trace, #1F2421); border: 1px solid rgb(31 36 33 / 0.32); border-radius: 0; padding: 4px 8px; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-trace, #1F2421); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Orb
components.description: Player identity as shape, not just color — disc / ring / diamond / triangle, one per player, always paired with that player's hue.
components.html: <svg class="ds-orb" viewBox="0 0 100 100" style="color:#2C5F87"><circle cx="50" cy="50" r="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="5"/></svg>

narrative.overview:
Chipfire's subject is a controlled detonation propagating through a lattice — accumulation, threshold, release. The visual world is not a game skin; it is the instrument that would actually sit in the room watching that happen: a seismograph and a blast-monitoring chart. A fine grid, ink traces, a station clock. Everything is precise and legible rather than arcade — no glow-for-its-own-sake, no celebratory chrome, no decoration that isn't also a reading. When the system needs to say something, it says it the way an instrument does: a mark, a number, a trace left on the paper — never a badge or a burst of color.

The system runs in exactly two states, never a blend. By day it is chart paper: cream stock, a hairline-printed grid, dark ink. By night it is the station's own display, which is emissive rather than reflective — the palette folds in on itself (today's ink becomes the raised surface, today's paper becomes the ink) rather than being replaced by an invented dark theme.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, printed-paper materiality — a hairline lattice exists before any game state does.
Zero border-radius on every container, button, card, and input; roundness is reserved for data points only.
One saturated hue per player, and saturated color appears nowhere else.
Motion is a reading, not decoration — cascades propagate in event order, trembling encodes real danger, afterglow does not animate.
Space Grotesk for display and every numeral, IBM Plex Sans for prose, IBM Plex Mono for anything copied character-by-character.

rules.name: The One-Hue-Per-Player Rule
rules.body: Saturated color exists in this system for exactly one purpose — telling players apart. It never decorates a button, a chart axis, an icon, or a piece of chrome.

rules.name: The Shape-Before-Color Rule
rules.body: Every player color is paired with a distinct orb silhouette and every UI element that names a player repeats both. Color-vision deficiency must never cost a player the ability to read the board.

rules.name: The One Weight Above Rule
rules.body: A panel's title sits exactly one visual step above the label-micro fields inside it — sentence case and the display face, not louder tracking.

rules.name: The One Overlay Rule
rules.body: Only a true modal (a native dialog) gets a lift shadow. Everything else that needs to read as above its neighbor does so with a deeper paper tone or a border.

rules.name: The Sharp-Edged Rule
rules.body: Radius is zero everywhere except an actual data point (a capacity dot, a bar's flowing edge). A rounded corner on a container is always a mistake in this system.

dos: Do keep every container, button, card, and input at zero border-radius.
Do express raised or grouped with chart-deep tone and a hairline border, never a drop shadow.
Do pair every player-color usage with that player's orb shape.
Do use the numeral font (Space Grotesk, tabular figures) for every counter, score, and hash-adjacent number.
Do keep saturated color scoped to the four player hues and the brand mark's rust core.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: any animation above trivial must degrade to an instant, fully-informative state.
donts: Don't introduce a second raised-surface tone beyond Chart Stock and Chart Stock Deep.
Don't use Signal Rust (the mark's core) as a player color.
Don't animate the afterglow or add a decay effect to it.
Don't add a shadow, glow, or gradient fill to a button, card, or panel.
Don't derive a cascade animation's duration from the speed setting — only the delay between generations should change.
